en: Collected Imperial Edicts and Memorials Presented to the Tripitaka Master of Great Discrimination, Rectitude, and Vast Wisdom, Posthumously Honored as Grand Minister (Sikong) during the Reign of Emperor Daizong.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Shi Yuanzhao of Ximing Monastery in Chang’an, the Capital. Volume One.
Preface to the Tripitaka Master of Da Xingshan Monastery of the Great Tang:
His name was Zhizang, and his title was Bukong Jingang (Amoghavajra).
In Sanskrit, he was called Amoghavajra.
He was originally a man from the Western Regions.
In the past, he served the Great Propagator of the Teachings, Vajra Tripiṭaka,
and received the transmission of the mantras.
In his twenty-fourth year, he adjusted his robes and requested further instruction.
After the Great Master passed away, he traveled again to the Five Indias,
where he thoroughly examined and perused all the Sanskrit texts of the *Yogācāra*, traveling extensively and surveying them in their entirety.
He then proceeded to the imperial capital;
at times he transformed beings in Hexi,
and at other times he returned to Guannei.
During the final years of the Tiānbǎo era, the Hu horsemen entered Guān. In the second year of Zhìdé, the capital and Luò were recovered.
The Venerable Master personally received the imperial decree and diligently established the ritual altar.
He served as an abhiṣeka master and was favored by the Emperor at the three court audiences.
He composed one hundred and forty-four poems in response to imperial edicts sent to express gratitude, following the tradition of master and disciple succession.
It has thus been divided into six fascicles,
so that it may be circulated for future generations;
let those who delight in learning understand this intention.
A Memorial for the Celebration of the Recovery of the Western Capital during the Reign of Emperor Suzong; a Reply to the Memorial Celebrating the Recovery of the Eastern Capital;
a Reply to the Memorial Celebrating the Return of the Retired Emperor to the Capital; a Memorial of Personal Petition Expressing Gratitude for the Bestowal of Incense;
and an Imperial Decree Ordering the Search for Buddhist Scriptures Throughout the Realm for Repair and Translation, followed by the Decree Granting Permission for the Search.
A Visit to the Department of Buddhist Scriptures (Fanjiacibu) for a Notification (Gao-die); One Memorial (Zha) Congratulating Empress Zhang;

An Imperial Decree (Zhi) Granting Permission to Translate Sūtras and Śāstras along with a Notification from the Department of Buddhist Scriptures; A Statement in Response to the Presentation of a Gypsum Image and Sanskrit Texts Requesting the Transmission of True Mantras (Zhenyan);
and an Imperial Edict in Cursive Script (Mo-chi) Granting Permission to Establish an Initiation Hall (Guanding Daochang) at Daxingshan Monastery.
One decree appointing the Chief Commander of the Imperial Armies to perform meritorious deeds at Zhiju Monastery;
one memorial submitted by Emperor Daizong regarding the presentation of a white sandalwood image of Mārīcī along with the Sanskrit *Mahāpratisarā Dhāraṇī*;

one imperial edict in response to the request for the annual establishment of an empowerment ritual site (*abhiṣeka-maṇḍala*); and one petition requesting the establishment of Great Virtuous Monks (*bhadanta*) at Daxingshan Monastery.
One edict (zhìshū) requesting that forty-nine monks be ordained on the Emperor’s birthday;

one imperial decree from the Ministry of Rites (Cíbù) granting permission for the re-translation of the *Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* (*Rénwáng Bōrě Jīng*) according to the Sanskrit manuscript;

one edict by Du Mǎn, Vice Minister of the Censorate, requesting that his official seal be returned to the Translation Institute; and a letter of thanks for the Imperial composition of the new *Benevolent Kings Sūtra*.
Preface and Petition for Celebration of the Hundred Seated Assembly upon Seeing the Auspicious Clouds (1);
Imperial Decree Granting Posthumous Titles to the Late Vajra Tripiṭaka Master Kāi-fǔ (1); Imperial Decree Appointing Amoghavajra as Great Minister and Bestowing a Title (1);
Petition for Celebration of the Recovery of the Western Capital (1); Da Xingshan Monastery.
The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Zhizang said:
"I have humbly heard that Heaven alone is great."
Without a primordial sage, there would be no one to follow Heaven’s will in inflicting punishment;
only the King models himself after Heaven.
Without a founding king, there would be no one to replace Heaven in nurturing all things.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty’s merit transcends the establishment of the Pole Star,
and your Way surpasses the Primordial Chaos.
You have succeeded to the precious chart of Yao.
Furthermore, continuing the great achievements of Yu,

since the supreme villain was already eliminated some time ago, those who remain rebellious and deluded have yet to realize it. Your Majesty has waited with righteousness for them to turn their weapons against one another,
while first extending the grace of clemency.
May the bear-like warriors exert themselves for a time to forever exterminate the jackals and wolves.

From the capital, as the imperial precincts are cleared and purified, we look toward the palace towers for Your Majesty’s auspicious arrival; may Your Majesty graciously comply with the desires of the people.
Heaven’s will was fulfilled;
the mountains and rivers did not shift,
and the gardens remained as they were before.
Now that the imperial carriage has descended and the sacred governance is renewed,
you are about to manifest a response to the Great Heaven and bring salvation through benevolence and longevity,
leading forth the congratulations of the Former Sovereign at the banks of the Fen River.
Resembling the altar of the Supreme God’s Round Mound,
he turns the Wheel of Dharma throughout kalpas as numerous as grains of sand;
he illuminates the thousand worlds, suspending the Buddha-sun in the sky.
The Treasury of Wisdom has long been bathed in the King’s transformative influence;
now beholding the Han rites once more,
his life has already been abundantly fulfilled.
In repaying your grace, what hope can I harbor?
I am overwhelmed by the utmost sense of gratitude, like a duck or a water plant.
I respectfully approach the Silver Terrace Gate.
I respectfully submit this memorial to announce my congratulations;
for having thus lightly troubled Your Majesty’s august presence,
I am deeply filled with trepidation and anxiety.
The śramaṇa Zhizang, with the utmost reverence and trepidation, respectfully submits this address.

On the twenty-fourth day of the tenth month in the second year of the Zhide era, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Zhizang of Daxingshan Monastery presented this memorial to Emperor Ganyuan Guangtian Dashing Wenwu Xiaogong, who posthumously conferred upon him the imperial title of Emperor Wencming Wude Dashing Dashen Xiaogong.
This crafty faction has long been cruel and violent;
Heaven has grown weary of their calamity.
In the end, he was defeated and perished;
yet looking back upon the city walls and gates, they remained as they were,
and facing the officials and commoners, they all appeared unchanged.
My gratitude and consolation are profound and dwell deeply within my heart.
I acknowledge your congratulations.
A Memorial on the Joyful Reception of the Recovery of Dongjing. One memorial on the joyful reception of the recovery of Dongjing, submitted by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Zhizang of Daxingshan Monastery:
I humbly receive the news that Your Majesty’s army has achieved victory and recovered Dongjing.
The rebel faction melted away like ice,
and the royal army alone achieved victory.
The living beings rejoiced in such celebration that they leaped for joy, losing all sense of composure.
Upon hearing this, Zhizang said:
"That those who oppose virtue perish and their calamities cannot be avoided is recorded upon bamboo leaves;
this is truly a time-honored maxim."
Since the mad Hu barbarians threw China into chaos,
nearly three years have passed;
the spirits are resentful and the people are indignant.
As the evil had matured and the transgressions were full to overflowing, Your Majesty took little sleep, eating but sparingly even of the simple wine and meal.

Consequently, your ministers exerted their full strength and the martial forces vied with one another to take the lead; thus, no divine strategy was left unexecuted and no spiritual merit remained unachieved.
Riding upon this momentum like splitting bamboo,
we shall meet those who have turned their weapons against us;
with a single campaign, we shall achieve three victories.

Within ten days, the two capitals were both restored; indeed, there was no one who did not acknowledge that his sagely plans were widely applied and his brilliant strategies were extraordinary, such that his sacred power in sustaining and upholding [the realm] far surpassed that of all other sovereigns.
Now, as you are about to diligently honor Mount Dai in the east and manifest your offerings to the Supreme Mystery, I,
Zhizang, am fortunate to preserve this era of prosperity and brightness and look forward to witnessing these magnificent rites.
I cannot contain my boundless joy.
I respectfully approach the Silver Terrace Gate to present this memorial of congratulation for your perusal.
I fear having lightly troubled Your Majesty’s august presence.
I prostrate myself in deep trepidation.
The śramaṇa Zhizang, truly joyful and delighted,
respectfully submits this statement on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month in the second year of the Zhide era.

Memorial Submitted by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Zhizang of Daxingshan Monastery; Imperial Response Acknowledging the Congratulations. A Memorial Congratulating the Retired Emperor on His Return to the Capital.

One Memorial Congratulating the Retired Emperor on His Return to the Capital. Spoken by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra: [The Emperor’s response: "I have received your memorial offering congratulations. I acknowledge your congratulations. [The Memorial: "Śramaṇa Amoghavajra addresses the following: [Your Majesty has graciously permitted me to submit this memorial to congratulate Your Majesty upon your return to the capital.]"
Bukong replied: "I have heard that the Way is the precursor of the Emperor; when the Way of the Emperor is pervasive, divine efficacy acts without a presiding master.
Filial piety is the root of virtue."
Your supreme virtue has flourished, enabling you to receive the Great Mandate.
We humbly submit that Your Majesty, having received Heaven’s charge, continues the legacy of Yao;
following the will of the people, you restore the way of Yu.
Without altering a single thing, the Two Polarities were brought into harmonious contemplation;
before a full day had passed, both capitals were settled in peace. His virtue reached up to the Great Heaven and surpassed that of all sovereigns;
he received the homage of the multitude of lords from the east.
He went westward to welcome the Retired Emperor.
Shedding his imperial robes, he once again guided the imperial carriage;
purifying the celestial steps, he continued to extend his dharma-greetings. As Father of Heaven and Son of Heaven, he preceded heaven and followed heaven.
Having departed from the Gate of the Lofty Void (Chāng-hé), he returned once more to the Ninefold Palace;
he rectified the celestial framework and brought peace to the myriad subjects.

This was truly because His Majesty the Retired Emperor bestowed his teachings and deferred his merit to a height surpassing even the August Sovereign; and Your Majesty, seizing the opportune moment, has established supreme virtue that stands at the head of all kings who have risen to power.
It is sufficient to illuminate the annals of history and bring forth brilliance comparable to the eras of Tang and Yu;
it is not in vain that I have lived to witness this prosperity,
having happened to behold such a magnificent spectacle.
Unable to contain the height of my joy,
I have respectfully approached the Yintai Gate to present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
I have lightly touched upon Your Majesty’s august presence;
I am deeply moved with trepidation.
I, the śramaṇa Amoghavajra, speak these words with sincere joy and delight.

On the ninth day of the twelfth month in the second year of Zhìdé, Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Dàxīngshàn Monastery presented this memorial to the Emperor, who issued this decree: "The miasmic vapors have been swept away, and the realm has been brought to stability."
His Majesty has returned to his palace to reside in peace;
as we perform our morning and evening rites, our joy and celebration are profound indeed.
We acknowledge your congratulations.

A Memorial of Gratitude for the Bestowal of Incense and a Statement of Petition. One Memorial of Gratitude for the Bestowal of Incense and a Statement of Petition. Submitted by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra.
Imperial Messenger Wu Youyan arrived and respectfully proclaimed the Sacred Edict.
Since we have prepared this vegetarian feast at our monastery today,
we have been granted this special incense and the honor of Your Majesty’s celestial messenger descending upon us.
Having been graced by such vast kindness,
my joy is beyond description;
I am truly glad and truly delighted.
Amoghavajra entrusted himself to the protective shade of the Dharma-stream,
intending to propagate the Esoteric Teachings;
thus he traveled alone across ten thousand li.
He studied extensively throughout the five regions of India;
with focused contemplation upon the ten directions, he beheld the Buddhas of the Flower Treasury World,
and through single-minded devotion to the five families of mantras, he mastered the true words of the Nairañjanā Grove.
Each time they arrange the characters, contemplate the mind, and cast themselves down to request protection,
they vow that by the power of his great vows,
they may encounter the appearance of a Wheel-Turning King.
For ten years, with pure sincerity,
he repeatedly encountered the enlightened sage.
In previous years, when the Pass of the函 (Hanguan) had not yet opened, Your Majesty was cultivating virtue in the Spring Palace.
I have long since received your gracious decree,
which has kindly bestowed upon me your inquiries,
as well as the gift of incense and medicine.
He secretly dispatched consecrated [objects].
Furthermore, when Your Majesty traveled north,
although Amoghavajra was unable to attend upon you, [he remained devoted].
The disciple Seng Han-guang and others followed [the Emperor] from the west;
upon emerging, they were again granted the privilege of attending the imperial carriage as it traversed the rugged terrain amidst the military ranks.
I have been granted prior audience regarding the deliberations on the imperial edict.
Although Amoghavajra’s body is trapped within the lands of the Hu,
his mind has always remained devoted to the imperial court.
I have repeatedly received secret edicts;
my offerings have all reached [the Emperor]. Your Majesty’s sagacious plans are exercised alone, and the power of the Dharma adds its support from the unseen.
The host of wicked ones has been dispersed and eliminated, and the celestial omens have returned to their proper order.
I, of insignificant substance,
have once again been graced by the imperial bounty.
In the tenth month, the palace was purified to establish an assembly for the expulsion of demons; on the first day of the lunar month,
he again presided over the altar of consecration to offer prayers for the imperial title,
while the upper palace was adorned with decorative coatings.
He cultivated his practice in a separate hall.
Having been granted permission to translate scriptures, he was further bestowed with the profound grace of ordaining monks; thus, the imperial favor was already deep.
When shall I be able to repay this kindness?
I shall reverently bathe the images at the three times of the day and perform *homā* every half-month,
so that the thirty-seven honored ones may protect the realm of the King of Enlightenment.
The sixteen protective deities increase, and the majestic spiritual power of the Sage Emperor is such that his life shall be as eternal and boundless as the Southern Mountains.
We are all overcome with the utmost joy and gratitude.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge of it.
I, the śramaṇa Amoghavajra, speak with sincere joy and delight.

On the twenty-third day of the first month of the third year of Zhide, at Daxingshan Monastery, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra presents this memorial to Emperor Gaozong Wenwu Dashing Xiaogang. The Emperor’s reply: "The Master has manifested his presence in the Western Land."
The opening of the Dharma in the Middle Kingdom—
your past great vows—
I know them all in my heart.
Having performed walking meditations as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
he has attained great power of merit.
Since the time we have been traveling on foot, [we have encountered...]
Constantly mindful of causes and conditions,
this bhikṣu now seeks the Way and extends his vow. Now,
upon these most pure lotuses and layered palmyra leaves, he proclaims the subtle and wondrous, inconceivable Buddha-dharma.
To revere that which is free from obstruction is to offer powdered incense.
To uphold and practice with diligence, never regressing,
is what I wish to inform you of.

An Imperial Edict: We command that all Sanskrit manuscripts throughout the realm be sought out, restored, and translated. Furthermore, we decree that the Sanskrit manuscripts within the Ci'en and Jianfu Monasteries of the Central Capital be thoroughly examined, repaired, and translated. One edict. Issued from the Zhongjing (Central Capital). Ci'en and Jianfu Monasteries.
Furthermore, at temples such as Shōzen-ji, Chōju-ji, and Fukūkō-ji in Tōkyō, as well as in various provincial,
prefectural, and village monasteries,
there were Sanskrit manuscripts formerly brought by the Tripitaka masters Mahāvairocana (Yijing), Śubhakarasiṃha (Xuanwuwei), Paramārtha (Liuzhi), and Ratnasena (Baosheng).
The above is a memorial submitted by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple.
Regarding the aforementioned Sanskrit manuscripts and other texts,
he reports that there are many among the previous holdings of the Tripiṭaka that have not yet been translated.
The years and months having passed long, many of the cords have snapped;
that these [texts] have been submerged and scattered is truly pitiable.
If they are not repaired, I fear they will contravene the holy teachings.
Recently, I have received Your Majesty’s gracious decree permitting me to translate this work.
As the task requires thorough investigation and verification of its subtle teachings,
I hope that you will grant permission for me to consult and collect relevant materials wherever they may be found.
Among these, those that were damaged, deficient, or leaking were repaired according to their condition.
Those deemed capable of extensive propagation to assist the state and spread the transformation [of the Dharma] were to continue the translation and report it to the throne;
this would provide the most extraordinary merit for the Imperial Person. Having received the Imperial favor and permission, they requested that the matter be entrusted to the relevant authorities.

The Secretariat and Chancellery issue this notification to the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery. We hereby notify you that, in accordance with the Imperial Edict, your request is granted. This notification is issued pursuant to the Edict. On the twelfth day of the third month of the first year of the Qianyuan era, by special appointment, Cui Yuan, Acting Chancellor of the Secretariat; Miao Jinqing, Acting President of the Chancellery; Li [Surname], Minister of War and Grand Master for Honoring Peace; and Shen [Surname], Minister of the Court of Civil Office and Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Master for Honoring Peace, have jointly issued a decree authorizing the search for and collection of Sanskrit manuscripts (Sanskrit: *vaṃśa-patra*). One official document from the Ministry of Rites authorizes the search for and collection of Sanskrit manuscripts at Ci'en and other monasteries in the Central Capital, as well as at Shengshan and Changshou monasteries in the Eastern Capital.
Furthermore, throughout the prefectures, counties, monasteries, and villages,
there were Sanskrit manuscripts formerly brought by the Tripitaka masters Da-bian-jue (Wuxing), Yijing, Shihu (Śīlabhadra), Śubhakarasiṃha, and others.
The above was submitted by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery.
Regarding the aforementioned Sanskrit manuscripts and other texts,
he reports that there are many among them that have not yet been translated.
As many years and months have passed, many of the cords and straps have broken;
that these should now be buried in ruin and scattered about is truly lamentable.
If they are not repaired, I fear it will contravene the holy teachings.
Having recently received Your Majesty’s gracious command permitting its translation,
we seek to rely upon investigation and study to verify and comprehend these subtle words.
We hope that you will allow us to search for and collect the necessary materials wherever they may be found.
Among them, those that were damaged or incomplete were repaired according to their respective conditions.
Those deemed capable of propagating and expounding the teachings to assist the state in uplifting its transformation were to continue the translations and report them to the throne;

it was considered most excellent that such merit might benefit the Imperial Person. The Imperial Grace granted permission, and the matter was requested to be entrusted to the relevant authorities. By imperial decree, the request was granted.

The seventeenth day of the third month in the first year of the Qianduan era. The Clerk Meng Gui, on behalf of the Chief Administrator Tang Guoxing and the Vice Minister Wei Shaoyou, submits this memorial to congratulate Empress Zhang. One memorial congratulating Empress Zhang, addressed by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. [The Memorial] Śramaṇa Amoghavajra states: On the seventeenth day of the third month in the first year of the Qianduan era, the Emperor received the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* (The Lotus Sutra) translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda. On that very day, the Emperor personally performed the ritual of offering incense and flowers. He then issued a decree, stating: "The Buddha’s Dharma is profound and vast; its principles are subtle and far-reaching. It is the ultimate truth that transcends all worldly phenomena. Now, having obtained this sutra, it shall be enshrined within the palace. Let the Empress and the various consorts each offer incense and flowers to pay homage. Upon receiving this imperial decree, we, your humble subjects, were filled with joy and awe. We have heard that the Buddha’s teachings are the source of all blessings and the foundation of all peace. That the Emperor has now personally honored them with offerings demonstrates his profound devotion to the Triple Gem and his desire to bring benefit to the realm. We pray that through the power of these merits, the Emperor’s sagely virtue may increase daily, the state may enjoy eternal tranquility, and all sentient beings may attain liberation. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our congratulations. Respectfully submitted by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. I humbly observe the imperial decree of this auspicious day concerning the Empress.
I have humbly heard that with heaven and earth, all things are brought forth;
through the alternation of yin and yang, the Way is formed.
Thus, they bring about divine transformation among the myriad things and act as mothers who nurture the multitudes of the people;
in the past, emperors and kings have regarded this as a magnificent and solemn rite.
I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, the Empress, has manifested virtue through the model of gentleness and assisted in the inner chambers of spring.
Beholding the vapors of the clouds, I know where my ultimate refuge lies.
As you stand at the military chariot and hand over the command of the army, Your Majesty responds above to the Mandate of Heaven and accords below with the Yin Virtue of the Earth;
you follow the hearts of the common people and act as the mother of the world.
The two images having been completed, ten million auspicious signs shall surely manifest.
Among all those within the realm, who would not offer praise and celebration?
How much more so for Amoghavajra, who has received special instruction in the Way?
Having long been bathed in profound grace,
my feelings of joy and exultation are ten thousand times greater than those of ordinary beings.
I cannot bear to restrain my utmost joy and trepidation.
I respectfully submit this congratulatory message for your perusal.
Amoghavajra, in profound humility and awe, speaks thus.

On the eighth day of the fourth month in the first year of the Qianyuan era, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple submitted this memorial to Emperor Guangwen Wudasheng Xiaogang. The Emperor’s decree read: "The Queen’s virtue extends throughout the palace."
Having achieved success in assisting [the Sovereign],
you have employed the most exalted rites to rectify the image of Kun (Earth). We acknowledge your congratulations.

An official edict from the Sacrificial Bureau authorizing the translation of scriptures and treatises, consisting of one document authorizing the translation of eighty works, including the *Dhāraṇī-śāstra* and the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-sūtra*.
Twenty Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna sūtras and śāstras, totaling one thousand two hundred fascicles.
The above was submitted by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple.
Amoghavajra has heard that those who succeeded Emperor Yao inherited the imperial throne.
Those who received the Buddha’s entrustment transmitted the Buddhist teachings;

Thus, Vajra Tripiṭaka possessed an exceptionally refined natural endowment;
his temperament was imbued with profound harmony,
and his insight penetrated the four modes of birth.
His mind was grounded in the six perfections.
Thus, from the Western Regions, he came to the East carrying his staff and alms-bowl;
with pure conduct encompassing his person and a compassionate heart aiding all beings.
The flower of awakening shines outwardly;
the torch of wisdom illuminates within.
It draws forth and leads all who are lost in delusion.
Having realized the penetration of perfect nirvana,
he secretly transmitted the seal of the Dharma and manifested nirvana through concealment.
The robes and alms-bowl remain empty;
his voice and presence have long departed.
Yet his teachings are able to endure for posterity.
Rituals provide adornment for the end of life;
it is fitting to honor his noble name so that his glory may be fully realized.
He shall be posthumously conferred the title of Kai-fu-yi-tong-san-si.
He was further conferred the title of *Dahongjiao Sanzang* (Tripitaka Master Great Propagator of the Teaching).

By nature he manifested *tathatā*;
having mastered the profound secret treasury,
he inherited the sublime intent of the Azure Garden and revealed the four reliances.
Translating the subtle words from the Golden Mouth, you serve as a bridge for the six realms of existence;
carrying the Dharma-casket upon your person, you traveled far across the shifting sands,
causing the transmission of the lamp to shine ever more brightly.
The nectar of immortality moistens all extensively;
the clouds of compassion are dispersed over the burning house,
and the sun of wisdom is raised upon the dark paths.
Recently, I personally inquired about the supreme causes;
you have extensively demonstrated the skillful means to forever resolve the net of doubt,
thereby nourishing the sprouts of my understanding.
Although the hearts that have transcended the mundane world have equally renounced fame and rank,
the rites of honor and exaltation serve to signal the virtues of the sages and philosophers; thus,
let them respond to this auspicious mandate so as to harmonize with the statutes of the court.

Therefore, the Great Preceptor Vajra Tripitaka Master shall be posthumously conferred the title of Kaifu Yitong Sansi,
and further granted the honorary title of Dahrongjiao (Great Propagator of the Teaching) Tripitaka Master.
Amoghavajra was specially promoted to the trial position of Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and was further granted the title of Tripitaka Master of Great and Vast Wisdom.
Like a single rain falling from heaven, its moisture flowed through both roots and leaves.
The radiant halo of his perfect brow emitted a brilliant light that illuminated both the realms of darkness and clarity.
Holding [the image] aloft, he paced back and forth, his heart filled with a mingling of sorrow and joy;
Amoghavajra was truly fearful and truly joyful, both piteous and apprehensive.
Bukong replied:
"The Ten Epithets are distinguished titles that manifest his virtues;
the Nine Ministers are positions of great importance, modeled after the nine rivers."
Therefore, the Great Upādhyāya’s Way permeated the transmission of the lamp;
it was truly intended to manifest his enduring legacy.

Those of us who do not possess the Dharma of non-emptiness yet presume to succeed our predecessors and share in this vast imperial bounty are like "swallow-stones" (ordinary pebbles) that mingle with precious gems,
or like those who play the flute out of tune while standing alongside the masters of the *qí* bamboo.
Honor extends to both the living and the deceased;
favor reaches even the teacher and his disciples.
We receive these gifts with trepidation and awe, gazing upon your words with faces flushed with shame.
How much more so for those who have left the household life and cast off their finery,
fundamentally forgetting both honor and disgrace,
and offering pure sincerity in service to the state.
The Sangha follows universal norms, yet Your Majesty, in the vast turning of the Golden Wheel,
graciously accepts even the discarded shards and rubble;
you have thus invited those who dwell in meditation into the inner palace.
Although I am as powerless as one who carries a mountain, I have been honored by following in his footsteps as a close guest, receiving the extraordinary rites of distinction and praise.
Thus, he diminished the flow of the Dharma’s lofty tradition and marked the pure footsteps of those with few desires;
for this reason, he personally submitted three petitions of refusal.
My words have been prolix before Your Majesty;
I hope that You will regard my earnest sincerity with profound reflection.
How could it be that [my resolve] is so firm as to be unshakable?
A young child in a sheep-cart feels abashed before vast wisdom and stands bewildered;
one of humble talent from the Deer Park is deeply ashamed before the Grand Minister of Reception.
I am unable to express the utmost depth of my gratitude.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for your imperial decree.
I, the śramaṇa Amoghavajra, am both deeply apprehensive and truly joyful.
Respectfully stated on the fifth day of the eleventh month of the first year of the Yongtai era.

A Memorial Submitted by the Special Advancement (Tejin), Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial (Hongluqing), Tripitaka Master of Great Vast Wisdom, and Śramaṇa of Xingshan Monastery, Amoghavajra; Imperial Response from Emperor Baoying Yuansheng Wenwu: "Venerable Master."
The Way is esoteric within the twin śāla trees, and its merit transcends that of perfect enlightenment.
Having traveled afar from India, the true mantras have been disseminated;
recently, I have attained refuge and personally received the entrustment.
The rites for honoring and exalting [the deceased] are of primary importance;
thus, the glory of the official seal and ribbon is increased,
thereby solemnizing the reverence due to teachers and guides.
I also hereby extend this gift of honor, hoping thereby to manifest the posthumous glory [of the deceased].

**Imperial Edict Requesting the Relinquishment of Robes and Alms-Bowl to Assist Monk Daohuan in the Repair of Jinguesi Temple** One Edict: To the Right Dharma Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa of Jinguesi Temple on Mount Wutai.
A memorial submitted by the *tejin* (Special Advance) and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, Da Guangzhi Bukong:
Regarding the aforementioned temple, although the imperial calligraphy for its plaque has already been bestowed, the temple buildings have not yet been completed.
This accords with the sacred traces of Mañjuśrī seen at Mount Tai by the monk Daoyi of Quzhou in the twenty-fourth year of the Kaiyuan era.
It is named Kinkaku-in (Golden Pavilion Temple).
It consists of thirteen sections where the monastic community resides;
it is said that there are ten thousand people there.
The terraces, halls, gates, and towers were fashioned from this gold.
At that time, a copy of the design was submitted for internal review.
The common people throughout the realm all desired that the Geumgak-sa Temple be completed.
Who among men does not wish for this?
Thus, the monk Daohuan of Zhezhou was ordered to deliver daily offerings to the mountain,
so that he might admire the Master Chan’s realization of the Way and its principles.
With the aspiration to serve the State, I have constructed Kinkaku-ji according to the original plan.
The scale and layout of the buildings are exactly as they were envisioned.
This summer, the construction commenced, and all necessary materials and tools for the craftsmen have been personally procured.
As his years drew to a close, the former sage’s imperial plaque was fulfilled, and his realization of the Way and its principles reached a state of profound resonance.
Observing that this monk’s aspirations were no small matter,
some have said he was an emanation of Mañjuśrī sent to plant seeds of supreme merit.
Furthermore, there are five temple plaques for the Ling-shan Temples on Mount Wutai:
Qingliang, Huayan, Foguang, and Yuhua temples were completed first;
only Jin-ge Temple remained unfinished.
Since this is a sacred site,
who would not look upon it with reverence?
May you not begrudge the relinquishing of your robes and alms bowl to assist in establishing this great undertaking by providing the ritual ring for the path.
I have often feared that the year would not grant me the opportunity,
thereby failing my long-held aspiration;
yet I repeatedly submitted petitions, and by the grace of Heaven, my request was compassionately granted.
Now, with the sacred traces of Mañjuśrī and the holy ones as its core,
who other than Your Majesty could have constructed this Golden Pavilion?
For it is upon the ridgepoles and beams that a great hall relies for support.
The limbs and arms are what the sovereign entrusts;
together they form a single body and bring harmony to the myriad states.
Thus, the Golden Pavilion stands in sublime majesty.

Were it not for the prime ministers and high officials who supported him, the military officers who assisted him, the myriad ministers who continued their service, and the thousand functionaries who together honored him—
how else could the excellence of the relationship between sovereign and subject be manifested,
and how could the greatness of the Golden Pavilion be glorified?
The Venerable Śramaṇa Hanguang of Baoshou Monastery has returned from his mission to the Imperial Court and respectfully performs meritorious deeds.
We humbly hope that Your Majesty will graciously proclaim the Imperial Edict at the site where the monastery is being built, so that our sincerity may be fulfilled.
May the spirits of the myriad souls illuminate [the world] to bestow great fortune, peace, and tranquility upon the realm, and to protect and bless the Imperial Person.
If Your Majesty’s grace permits, we pray that this be issued to the relevant authorities for implementation.

Issued by: Yuan Zai, Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellor; Du Hongjian, Minister of the Gate and Chancellor; Wang Jin, Minister of the Gate and Chancellor; Li Shi, Acting President of the Council of State; Shi, Acting Right Vice-Presidency and Chancellor; Shi, Acting Left Vice-Presidency and Chancellor; and He Pingzhou Zhiguang, Grand Secretary. A Petition from He Pingzhou Zhiguang Congratulating on the Suppression of Zhou Zhiguang. Amoghavajra states: [...]
I humbly submit that Zhou Zhiguang,
having dared to betray the imperial decree,
has now exposed himself to heavenly punishment.
The accumulation of evil has brought about the destruction of the body, as evidenced by the tradition of beheading;
meanwhile, blessings flow throughout the land,
and joy accords with the spirit of the springtime.
This is because Your Majesty’s divine calculations have communicated in secret and your sagacious plans have been employed in mystery;
thus, before the warriors had yet displayed their valor,
the common people had already attained peace.
The realm became tranquil,
and the barbarians lost their ambition.
Thus we know that the power of the Sage-King ultimately achieved the merit of non-belligerence.
The compassion of the Benevolent King has ensured that all sentient beings have obtained their lives;
that I have not vainly received these abundant favors increases my joy and gratitude beyond measure.
I am filled with the utmost joy and celebration.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for your favor.
Amoghavajra is truly joyful and delighted; he respectfully concludes his address.

I humbly observe that the Hall of the Ten Thousand Bodhisattvas for Protecting the State at Huadu Monastery is based upon what was seen by Mañjuśrī on Mount Wutai; there,
clouds serve as chariots and elephants as mounts, amidst the chaotic columns and beams.
The radiance filled the hall, no different from the Golden Pavilion.
On the twenty-third day of the twelfth month of last year,
I received the imperial decree bestowing incense and proclaiming the oral edict.
I command the Venerable Master of Chanting, Bukong Jianze,

During each of the three long months of fasting,

Reflecting eternally upon the entrustment, I deeply cherish his illustrious legacy.
I offer this meager gift of fragrant tea and venture to express my humble thanks.

**Imperial Decree for Ordaining Three Monks on the Emperor’s Birthday** One decree from the Secretariat and the Chancellery: A notification to the Great and Widely Wise Amoghavajra (Bukong). Born in the year of the Dog, thirty years of age; a native of the country of Tuhuo Luo.
Recite the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
recite the Awakening of Faith;
recite the Bodhisattva Precepts Sūtra.

The Dharma-name Huìhóng requested to reside at Xīmíng Temple. He was forty-five years of age. A Meritorious Subject of the Bǎoyīng era, he held the rank of Commandant of the Imperial Guard (Wǔjiàowèi), serving as Acting Major General of the Right Yùlíng Army, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Upper Pillar State (Shàngzhúguó); he was granted the Purple Gold Fish Bag and was registered in Gāotíng Township, Tiānbǎo County, Liáng Prefecture.
The Dharma name was Huicheng.

He requested to reside at Huadu Monastery. His attendant was Cao Moha, a youth whose age was recorded as [blank], a native of Anning Township, Yongan Village, Wannian County, Jingzhao Prefecture; his father served as the head of the household.
Having recited one volume of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, his dharma-name is Huishun. [He has] resided at Qianfu Temple.
By imperial decree, it is hereby ordered that he be granted ordination and assigned to reside at the aforementioned temple. This notification is issued in accordance with the decree.

Imperial Edict. Memorandum dated the thirteenth day of the tenth month of the third year of the Dali era. To Yuan Zai, Minister of the Central Secretariat and Chief Councilor; Du Hongjian, Minister of the Palace Gate and Chief Councilor; Wang Jin, Minister of the Palace Gate and Chief Councilor; Li [Name], Minister of War and Chief Councilor; and the Grand Master of Ceremonies concurrently serving as Director of the Central Secretariat: We request that the East Pagoda Cloister of Guangtian Temple be established as a station for travelers to and from Mount Wutai. Regulations for Establishing the East Pagoda Cloister of Guangtian Temple as a Station for Travelers to and from Mount Wutai (one copy). The following items were cast by the Chan Master Huiyin of the East Pagoda Cloister of Guangtian Temple: one lacquered *dou* measure and one hundred and thirty copper *dou* measures. The above was submitted by the Special Advancement, Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Temple, Da Guangzhi Bukong.
Zou Huiyin was a disciple of Amoghavajra.
For the sake of the state, he cast the aforementioned bell to provide general offerings for the Holy Golden Pavilion Temple and other monasteries on Mount Wutai.
This is the temple where Huiyin resided.
I request that you provide the funds for casting great merit at Mount Tai,
as well as for the travel expenses and lodging for the assembly of monks who come and go.
Furthermore, please instruct Huiyin to escort the sacred image to Mount Tai.
May this serve as perpetual offerings,
so that blessings may support the imperial lineage and the Emperor’s life-span be boundless.

The above memorial was submitted by the Great Virtue of the Capital, the Special Advancement (Tejin), Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Tripitaka Śramaṇa of Daxingshan Monastery, Da Guangzhi Bukong, and others:
"We, who have humbly followed in the footsteps of the monastic community..."
Having long cultivated the pure conduct and practiced the translation of sacred scriptures,
he attained a profound understanding of the mysterious gate.
The Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva has extensively propagated the Mahāyāna Esoteric Teachings,
which now reside permanently at Mount Tai.
Blessings nourish the myriad people.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty, the Emperor, the Treasure-Response, Primordial Sage, Martial and Civil,
is in virtue one with Heaven and Earth.
Your brilliance rivals that of the sun and moon;
may your boundless blessings bring peace and well-being to all living beings.
We humbly entreat you that from this day forward...
It is mandated that within the dining halls throughout the world, a statue of Mañjuśrī shall be specially placed above Piṇḍola-bharadvāja to serve as the presiding elder (upādhyāya).
This is clearly and explicitly stated in various sacred scriptures.
Even the Tathāgatas of the *Saṃghāṭa-sūtra* still receive his instructions;
indeed, all who have left the household life ought to fold their robes in reverence before him.
Even Samantabhadra and Avalokiteśvara hold fly-whisks to serve him.
The Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas hold the broom and take their place at the rear;
this is the custom throughout the land of India,
and is not a matter of the humble views of the monastics.
It is further requested that this be made a permanent standard forever.
The Secretariat and the Chancellery issue this notification to the Ministry of Sacrifices, in accordance with the Imperial Decree: "The Great Holy Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Son of the Dharma King."
Possessing supreme majesty and virtue, you are the guide of all Buddhas;
you cleanse the eyes and minds of all living beings and bring peace and well-being to my myriad subjects.
This salvation is boundless;
yet there is no one to be venerated.
What shall people look up to?
The current petition submitted by the Virtuous Ones of the Capital is in perfect accord with the sacred scriptures;
the request should be granted according to this memorial.
To be followed accordingly. Imperial Decree. Original Notification.

Having long cultivated meditative concentration and wisdom, he swiftly attained realization in accordance with Yoga.
He traveled afar to visit Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa to personally pray for the Holy Path;
the Most Spiritually Responsive One surely answered him, and his profound resonance was thus communicated.
The realization of the mind through the metaphor of the blue lotus lies herein.

The Imperial Edict of the Thirteenth Day Ordering the Establishment of a Mañjuśrī Temple at Zhide Monastery in Taiyuan Prefecture One Edict from the Chancellery (Zhongshu Menxia): Memorandum to the Tripitaka Master of Great Universal Wisdom, Amoghavajra. [This memorandum] is issued in accordance with the Imperial Decree following the memorial submitted by the Tripitaka Master of Great Universal Wisdom, Amoghavajra, who holds the rank of *Tetjin* (Special Advance) and serves as Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial (*Honglu Qing*).
I request that a monastery for Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva be established at Zhide Temple in Taiyuan Prefecture,
and that twenty-one virtuous monks of the three studies be selected from among the clergy.
To propagate the fundamental teachings and continue the lamp of the Dharma,
you have requested that Dharma Master Daoxian reside at this monastery for an extended period to deliver lectures;
this request shall be granted in accordance with your memorial.
Issued in accordance with the Imperial Decree.

A notification dated the thirteenth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of the Dali era, addressed to Yuan Zai, Grand Secretary and Chief Councilor. Four seals are affixed above. On the fourth day of the ninth month of the same year, another hand-written edict was bestowed; on the fourth day of the ninth month of the same year, yet another hand-written edict was bestowed, one decree addressed to the Tripitaka Master of Great and Vast Wisdom.
Profoundly attuned to the source of the Way, he traveled afar to seek out sacred traces.
Through the wondrous power of his compassion, he manifested the True Doctrine:
once the five aggregates are empty, suchness remains as it is.
Venerable Huìqiū, I hope you have been well and at peace. This letter is brief.

On the fourth day, [I] requested the installation of an image in the Hàoling Hall at Tàiyuán Monastery and the selection of monks from Jìngtǔ Monastery according to the monastic regulations. Please install one set of images of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra at Hōreidō.
At the Kanjō Dōjō in Jōdoin,
please select fourteen monks to recite the Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī on behalf of the longevity of the nation.
The above is a memorial submitted by the Right Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra: "Previously,
having received Your Majesty’s gracious command,
I traveled to Mount Wutai to cultivate merit, reaching Taiyuan."
While on pilgrimage to the aforementioned temple,
I was able to behold the sacred traces of the righteous uprising of our High Ancestor and Emperor Taizong, all of which are located within this very temple;
it is truly the source from which the imperial enterprise of our nation arose.
This case certainly does not conform to the precedents of other monasteries.
We humbly pray that Your Majesty’s compassionate grace will remit all labor levies and land taxes,
and instead allocate these resources for our use.
On the memorial days of the seven successive sovereigns, beginning with Gaozu and Taizong, vegetarian feasts were established and incense was offered.
Furthermore, the Hall of Ritual Decrees was renovated and dedicated to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Additionally, during the three months of the Great Fast and on each of the ten days of fasting within those months, [the same rites were observed].

He ordered the monks of the entire monastery to recite the *Benevolent Kings Sūtra on the Perfection of Wisdom for the Protection of the State* on behalf of the seven successive sovereigns, from the High Ancestor (Gaozu) to Emperor Suzong,
so that they might obtain boundless merit to eternally support these seven sagely rulers.
May the inexhaustible sound of the Dharma accord with the Emperor’s longevity.
We humbly pray that you will carefully select those monks who perform recitations and record their names.
[The Emperor] decreed that lay visitors be halted first and dispatched immediately. The Chancellery and Secretariat issue this notification to the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra:

Notification in accordance with the Imperial Decree: "It is appropriate to act as requested. This notification is issued in accordance with the decree on the first day of the tenth month of the fifth year of the Dali era. Notification from Yuan Cai, Minister of the Interior and Chief Councilor; Wang Jin, Minister of the Secretariat and Chief Councilor; Li Nai, Minister of War and Chief Councilor; and the Grand Master of State and Chief Secretary of the Chancellery, all serving as Commissioners of the Court of the Imperial Household. A Petition Requesting Dharma Master Huilin to Preach at Baoshou Monastery. One Petition Requesting Dharma Master Huilin to Preach at Baoshou Monastery. Śramaṇa Amoghavajra states: [Text follows...]
Amoghavajra heard it not.
It was for the purpose of propagating the Śākya teachings that the sūtras were translated upon palm leaves;
it was for the purpose of entrusting [the Dharma] to the Heavenly Kings that the gāthās were expounded from the Lotus [Sūtra].
I humbly observe that Your Majesty’s station is as precious as the golden wheel,
while your mind roams within the jewel-like verses;
your filial virtue moves both Heaven and Earth.
Civilization is as equal to the sun and moon.
I humbly observe that the monk Huilin of Zhangjing Temple has possessed intelligence and insight since childhood and has resolved to transmit the lamp of the Dharma.
He expounds the Mahāyāna, thereby responding loftily to the great favors [of the state].
Constantly reciting these wondrous meanings,
he was able to proclaim and remember that land;
he was especially fortunate to receive the imperial grace.
I, Bukong, now respectfully request, on behalf of the state, that at Baoshou Monastery you expound the True Sūtra for both the clergy and the laity.
It is my hope that the holy mandate of the imperial ancestral temples may endure through great kalpas,
and that the field of merit for the common people may extend their years as high as Mount Sumeru.
As permitted by Your Majesty’s gracious favor, may it descend [as an imperial decree].
The edict was issued in accordance with the petition.

On the second day of the second month of the sixth year of the Dali era, the *tejin* (Special Advance) and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, submits this memorial to thank for the imperial gift of the *śīla-sūtra* and various scriptures, as well as provisions and rations for Daixingshan Monastery. Memorial of Thanks for the Imperial Gift of the *Śīla-sūtra* and Various Scriptures, as well as Provisions and Rations for Daixingshan Monastery. One Memorial submitted by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra: Amoghavajra says: [...]
The Imperial Messenger Li Xiancheng respectfully proclaimed the Sacred Edict:
"We specially bestow upon the Precept-Conferral Vaipulya Maṇḍala of Daxingshan Temple various provisions, including non-glutinous rice, glutinous rice, millet, oil, firewood, and other items."
Nothing was lacking,
and it was used to fully provide for the offerings of the fast;
holding them up in reverence, I felt a mingling of shame, trepidation, joy, and awe.
Furthermore, you have graciously granted me permission for my place of practice;
this is already a great fortune.
To grant me this additional offering of provisions for the monastics is even more so.
The grace of your benevolence is truly profound;
I am ashamed that I lack the means to offer a fitting response.
I shall merely apply myself with diligent effort day and night, increasing my practice of recitation.
I hope to repay even a ten-thousandth part [of their kindness].
I respectfully request that the assembly of monks who have received the precepts shall,
for twenty-one days, recite with sincere devotion and diligently practice the Way.
This is respectfully performed for the sake of the state to cultivate supreme merit;
may its boundless virtue serve to support the person of the Sovereign.
I am overcome with the utmost shame and gratitude.
I respectfully take this opportunity to submit a memorial through the imperial messenger Li Xiancheng to express my thanks to His Majesty.
The śramaṇa Amoghavajra, truly joyful yet fearful, speaks thus.

To inspire future students and nurture auspicious conditions—
this which has been bestowed is no small matter.
Regarding the matter of the petition:

A Memorial of Thanks for the Imperial Bestowal of Five Milch Cows with Calves by Chief Official Zhao Yi and Court Physician Dong Jin. A Single Memorial of Thanks for the Imperial Bestowal of Milch Cows, spoken by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. [The Emperor] has graciously bestowed upon me five Milch cows along with their calves. I, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, humbly submit this memorial to express my gratitude. I, [Name], am a humble monk of the Great Tang. Now, by imperial decree, I have been granted five Milch cows together with their calves. These animals are of great utility; they provide nourishment for the masses and serve as a source of sustenance for the people. Their milk can be used to prepare medicinal decoctions for the sick, thereby benefiting the populace. Furthermore, they may be employed to produce clarified butter for the lighting of lamps, which aids in the propagation of the Dharma. I am deeply moved by the Emperor’s profound benevolence and vast compassion. His grace extends even to such humble creatures, ensuring that they shall not suffer from hunger or thirst. This act of kindness is truly beyond measure. I, your servant, am filled with joy and prostrate myself in gratitude. I vow to diligently care for these animals, providing them with fodder and shelter so that they may thrive and fulfill their purpose. I hereby respectfully submit this memorial to express my heartfelt thanks for the imperial favor. I pray that the Emperor’s sagely virtue may endure forever and that his reign may bring peace and prosperity to all under heaven. Respectfully submitted by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. [Date] Chief Official Zhao Yi and Court Physician Dong Jin also submit this memorial to express our gratitude for the imperial bestowal. We humbly acknowledge the profound favor shown to us and pledge to ensure that these precious gifts are utilized to the utmost benefit of the state and its people. Respectfully submitted. [Date] *Note: The original text contains the phrase "乳牛五頭并犢" (five Milch cows with calves) and the title "沙門不空言" (spoken by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra).*
Today, I have been specially honored by Your Majesty’s decree,
granting me five milch cows, each with its calf.
Bestowed from Heaven, I am so overcome with awe and joy that I have no place to stand.
I, Bukong, am truly ashamed and deeply grateful;
I feel both joy and remorse.
I humbly reflect that Your Majesty, the Emperor, the Treasure-Response, Primordial Sage, Martial and Civil, is as majestic as the sun and moon, and your grace exceeds that of rain and dew.
Though I have been diligent throughout the four seasons, how could it repay even a ten-thousandth part?
To exhaust my strength and loyalty, I truly find it difficult to express my gratitude;
yet as I touch my heart and examine myself, I am filled with shame at my own shortcomings.
I am unable to bear the extreme depth of Your Majesty’s profound favor and kindness.
I respectfully submit this memorial to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
I, the śramaṇa Amoghavajra, with utmost reverence and trepidation, state this.

On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month in the sixth year of the Dali era, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Bukong, of Great Wisdom and Broad Insight, serving as Special Advancement and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial at Daxingshan Monastery, submitted this memorial to Emperor Baoying Yuansheng Wencu. The Emperor’s decree read: "The Venerable Master has profoundly penetrated the secret treasury."
Guarding and mindful with diligent sincerity,
you have applied yourself to refined cultivation;
it is fitting that you should receive this gracious mandate.
The favor bestowed is not slight; I trouble you to convey my profound gratitude for this kindness.

Spoken by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra: "Since my youth, I have served my late master, the Tripiṭaka Master Mahāvairocana, for twenty-four years."
Having received the yoga-dharmaparyāya,
he later traveled to Wufu to seek out those teachings he had not yet received, as well as various sūtras and śāstras,
where he studied them once again.
In total, more than five hundred sections of the Yoga Mantra Sūtras and Śāstras were obtained from Sanskrit manuscripts.
These holy words were respectfully translated in detail for the sake of the state,
so as to extensively promote blessings and protection.
In the fifth year of the Tiānbǎo era, he returned once more to the Capital.
By imperial decree from Emperor Xuānzōng,
he established a *daochǎng* within the palace.
He pledged to translate all the Sanskrit scriptures he had brought with him.
Furthermore, when Emperor Suzong— equal to Heaven and a successor to the sages—
ascended the throne, he specifically received an imperial edict.
Within the inner sanctuary, he established the rites of homa and empowerment.
Furthermore, he served as a state translator of scriptures to assist in proclaiming the imperial transformation.
I have repeatedly received imperial edicts from the two sagely sovereigns,
commanding that all Sanskrit manuscripts belonging to the Tripitaka masters of previous generations be sought out and collected; furthermore,
it was ordered that any where the cords or bindings had become loose or fallen apart should be immediately repaired.
Regarding those works that have not yet been translated, we shall continue to translate them and present them for Your Majesty’s consideration. We humbly pray that Your Majesty,
inheriting the imperial destiny and providing great protection to all sentient beings,
will extensively open up fields of merit.
The sun and moon are doubly bright;
the waves of grace extend afar;
the rain of Dharma flows in many streams.
The hearts of the four seas find their repose therein,
and the myriad regions rejoice in their veneration.
Thus we know that the Buddha’s entrustment truly rests upon Your Majesty, the Sage Ruler.
I, Bukū, have been undeservedly graced by your profound bounty; my sense of honor and fortune is truly deep.
I reflect earnestly upon how I might repay the state.
I shall uphold the sacred edicts of the late Sovereign and propagate his subtle teachings.
Furthermore, having received the gracious decree of Your Majesty and respectfully honored the final testament,
I have once again dispatched translators to bring benefit and salvation to all living beings;
yet, despite my diligent efforts throughout the four seasons, I have not repaid even a ten-thousandth part of [the debt].
For this reason, I have diligently devoted my days and nights to carefully translating mantras and Mahāyāna sūtras,
hoping to contribute even a tiny drop to the vast ocean.
This shall serve to support the Imperial Way.
The *Vajraśekhara Yoga Dharma-gate* that he translated is the swift path to Buddhahood;
its practitioners will surely be able to transcend ordinary realms instantaneously and reach the further shore.
The mantras of other schools and the expedient means of the various Buddhas are not uniform among their followers.
All the Mahāyāna sūtras translated [herein] serve as supreme provisions for the state and realm, pacifying and extinguishing calamities and misfortunes.
May the stars and constellations not err, and may wind and rain be regulated with care.
We look up in reliance upon the power of the Buddha to assist and perfect the state.
We have respectfully compiled and gathered all that has been translated previously and subsequently.
From the beginning of the Kaiyuan era until the sixth year of the Dali era,
there are a total of one hundred and one scrolls comprising seventy-seven works, including one scroll of the catalog;
the names of the monks and laypeople who received the dictation have been recorded, and the transcription is now complete.
I respectfully prepare and present this offering on the occasion of Your Majesty’s birthday,
praying that the blessings of the True Mantras may long protect Your Sacred Person,
and that the power of the Mahāyāna may forever preserve the realm.
Among those Sanskrit texts not yet translated,
I have continued to translate and submit for imperial review only those that protect the state and bring blessings and nourishment to the people.
Overwhelmed by the utmost sincerity, I respectfully present this memorial to inform Your Majesty.
The Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, with utmost reverence and trepidation, respectfully addresses Your Majesty.

On the twelfth day of the tenth month of the sixth year of the Dali era, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Da Guangzhi Amoghavajra, holding the special rank of *Tetjin* and serving as Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, presents this memorial to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, the Martial and Civilly Virtuous. The Emperor’s Imperial Rescript: "Your Reverence served the former dynasty from an early age, extensively propagating and elucidating the wondrous teachings."
Expounding upon these palm-leaf manuscripts, you have extensively shown the way for those lost in the dark.
As I succeed to the great throne, I reverently receive your sagely instructions;
may the Upādhyāya further refine and translate them with meticulous care.
To ensure that the scrolls are completed and continuously transmitted so as to eternally save all living beings is truly worthy of profound admiration.
These translated scriptures should be proclaimed and disseminated both within and beyond the borders.
A Petition of Gratitude for Permission to Include Newly Translated Sūtras and Śāstras in the Catalogue for Circulation.

One petition: Submitted by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra. I humbly submit this to express my gratitude for Your Majesty’s gracious permission to include the newly translated sūtras and śāstras in the catalogue of all scriptures for their circulation. [The text follows with the formal address and the body of the petition.]
The Imperial Messenger Li Xiancheng respectfully proclaimed the Sacred Edict:

"Send the catalog of newly translated scriptures, one imperial decree, and one edict in response to the memorial for the presentation of the scriptures; these are specially ordered to be implemented throughout the court and the realm."
I shall continue to include it in the catalogues of all the scriptures and carry it upon my head with the utmost reverence;
I am overwhelmed with joy and gratitude, feeling both sincere delight and profound trepidation,
sighing again and again in awe and shame.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty has inherited the mandate of the Dharma King;
you fulfill the aspirations of the hearts of men, uphold the secret seal of Samantabhadra,
and propagate the righteous teachings of the Son of Heaven.
Within a single day,
the bright sun of grace reaches across the eight directions;
in a mere instant, it pours forth a vast bounty upon all things.
This is indeed a source of supreme fortune for all under heaven, let alone for one such as Amoghavajra.

For over forty years, Amoghavajra has translated sacred scriptures; since the three successive reigns, he has devoted his will to propagating the merit of these translations, which he has assisted in cultivating.
Above, it shall support the royal house; below, it shall nourish all living beings.
Who would have thought that my lifelong aspiration would be fulfilled in a single day?
The Sage’s grace is so vast that it can hardly be repaid throughout kalpas.
How much more so, then, that you have specifically granted permission to translate those Sanskrit manuscripts that have not yet been translated;
this redoubles my sorrow and joy.
I venture to exhaust my mind and strength to carry out your sacred command.
I continue to translate and present this for Your Majesty’s perusal.
Overwhelmed by joy and trepidation, my gratitude is boundless.
I respectfully entrust this memorial to the Imperial Messenger Li Xiancheng to inform Your Majesty.
Bukong, filled with sincerity, joy, and shame, respectfully submits these words.

On the twenty-seventh day of the first month of the seventh year of the Dali era, Bukong—of the rank of Special Advancement (Tejin), serving as Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial (Hongluqing), and Tripitaka Master of Great Universal Wisdom—presents this memorial to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, Martial and Civilly Virtuous. The Emperor’s decree reads: “The Upādhyāya has long since realized Bodhi and entered into the Buddha’s knowledge and vision.”
All the translated scriptures thoroughly penetrate the subtle and profound; having received his mandate,
he promulgated the rites and practices to transmit their illuminating grace throughout the world,
bestowing them upon the entire realm to extensively save all sentient beings.
I have not yet been able to illuminate the Compassionate Vessel; I trouble you to convey my thanks.

Imperial Edict Granting the Nameplate for the Buddha Hall Temple of Xiyuanfang in Xihe County, Fenzhou. [Imperial Edict] Granting the Nameplate for the Buddha Hall Temple of Xiyuanfang in Xihe County, Fenzhou. One edict: The Ancient Buddha Hall Courtyard of Xiyuanfang in Xihe County, Fenzhou.
The above memorial was submitted by the Right Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Tripitaka Master Da Guangzhi Bukong.
Regarding the aforementioned Buddhist hall,
the common people of the local community in Xihe County [have petitioned].
In the Zhide era, they first formed a vow to jointly restore and repair it.
When the malevolent rebels were exterminated and the state was reclaimed, [the work was completed].
I humbly submit that the former Sage took filial piety as the name for his shrine;
he neither troubled the public administration nor did he privately seek alms.
The members of that community each contributed their own resources, and together they completed the restoration.
Since then, the repairs have been carried out without interruption.
Last year, we received an imperial decree.
While performing meritorious deeds at Mount Wutai,
he returned one day to this Buddha Hall courtyard;
upon inquiring into its origins, he came to know the full details of its reality.

The halls, pavilions, and courtyards are already completed and nearing final perfection. I particularly hope for Your Majesty’s gracious favor to grant a temple plaque.
