I respectfully entrust this memorial of thanks to Wei Mingxiu, an official of the Office of Supervisors, to present it for Your Majesty’s perusal.
The śramaṇa Huixiao, with the utmost reverence and trepidation, respectfully addresses these words.

On the nineteenth day of the third month in the twelfth year of the Dali era, the śramaṇa Huixiao, Director of Merit Cultivation at Wutai Mountain and monk of Ximing Monastery, submits this memorial to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, Martial and Civilly Virtuous. The Imperial Rescript: "The Master has taken refuge in the Śramaṇa Gate."
He widely propagated the holy teachings;
as he sought them through words and forms,
he was about to depart for Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.
The bestowed gifts were not many;
do not trouble yourself with a formal expression of thanks.

An imperial decree has been issued for you to perform meritorious deeds together with Huilang. [Attached is] one memorial of thanks for the imperial decree regarding the performance of meritorious deeds with Huilang, along with a reply to the śramaṇa Huixiao.
On the eleventh day of the third month,
I received your instructions in person,
ordering that meritorious deeds be performed at Mount Wutai.
On the nineteenth day of the seventh month, after the midday meal,
he went on a pilgrimage with over seventy people, including the imperial messenger Li Tongzhi and others,
carrying incense and candles.
The fire I have brought cannot reach the terrace.
I reproach myself with all my heart:
upon what basis can I venture to make this request?
When the youth Biange reached the summit of the mountain,
he suddenly saw damp ashes upon a rock; from these,
he was able to obtain a small spark of fire.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty’s imperial influence reaches even the most remote places;
the sacred fire has been kindled from damp ashes.
As incense is burned and prayers are offered, [may this merit be dedicated].
The Bodhisattva manifested in ten thousand forms;
his radiance was brilliant and resplendent,
and his marks and signs were distinct and clear.
It remained motionless, filling the sky,
and did not dissipate until evening.
Furthermore, he went to this terrace together with the supervising official Wei Mingxiu and others.
While offering prayers for the sake of the nation, as he was making his vow,
the Bodhisattvas Śarīraprabha and Maṇḍalaprabha appeared in succession twenty-seven times as manifestations.
Your Majesty’s sacred resonance operates in profound stillness,
and the Bodhisattva has manifested repeatedly;
the auspicious portents at Mount Wutai resulting from your veneration are manifold.
How fortunate this humble monk is to behold such sacred traces!
I am overcome with the utmost sense of gratitude and joy.
On the tenth day of this month, I received the grace of Heaven.
He was ordered to perform meritorious deeds together with Huìlǎng at every occasion;
by the Emperor’s extraordinary favor,
he was again admitted into the precious halls of the Golden Gate to engage in spiritual cultivation.
I am filled with boundless trepidation.
I respectfully enclose this memorial of thanks to be presented through the imperial envoy Li Xiancheng for Your Majesty’s knowledge.
The śramaṇa Huixiao expresses his sincere joy and delight. Respectfully stated.

On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month in the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the śramaṇa Huixiao of Ximing Monastery, acting as the Commissioner for Cultivating Merit at Mount Wutai, submitted this memorial to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, the Martial and Civilly Virtuous. The Emperor’s decree read: "The Master has served with diligence in the Brahma-conduct."
Having long resided at Qingliang,
his karma was vast and his precepts perfect;
his will was refined and his accomplishments complete.
Together we shall present this petition for purification;
may blessings be heaped upon our family and state.
I trust you will understand my thanks.

A Memorial Presenting a *Cintāmaṇi* Jewel on the First Day of the New Year; one memorial presenting a *cintāmaṇi* jewel on the first day of the new year, together with a response to the śramaṇa Huìxiǎo.
I have humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious decree.
He ordered the Tai Shan monastery to inspect and repair meritorious works for the sake of praying for blessings upon the state;
he reached the Southern Terrace (Nan Tai),
where there was a mountain to the south.
Previously, when a certain Indian monk was on pilgrimage,
he remarked that this mountain contains *cintāmaṇi* jewels; however,
those whose minds are overcome by greed will all encounter wind and thunder.
Hui-xiao burned incense and prayed to ascend this mountain.
There was a small stone cave several feet square,
containing water the color of vermilion.
Within it, he obtained thirty pieces of treasure;
those whose color was like amber were given to Huixiao for him to hear.
When the Sage King was moved by resonance,
the earth did not conceal its treasures.
We humbly reflect that Your Majesty’s encompassing and supporting of all things is like that of Heaven and Earth.
It illuminates like the sun and moon;
how much more so when a golden pavilion towers beneath the peaks and a jade-flowered hall is constructed upon the mountain ridges.
I, a humble monk, have received this mandate to ascend that famous mountain;
yet as I burned incense and invoked my sincerity,
lightning and rain did not fall.
Thus, he obtained this treasure.
Furthermore, according to the *Parnirvāṇa Sūtra*, it says:
"He stepped with his foot upon a single stone on Mount Tai."
For seven kalpas thereafter, one shall not fall into the evil realms;
how much more so for this rare treasure of an extraordinary age,
on this day when all things are renewed.
On this occasion of receiving the divine protection of the Ninefold Heavens,
I respectfully submit this with the accompanying imperial envoy, Li Xiancheng, to present it for Your Majesty’s perusal.
The Sramana Huixiao, in profound trepidation and joy, speaks thus.

On the first day of the first month in the thirteenth year of the Dali era, Huixiao, a śramaṇa of Ximing Monastery and Commissioner for Cultivating Merit at Mount Wutai, presented this memorial. An imperial edict from Emperor Baoying Yuansheng Wenwu was issued: "The Master has sought the Way on the Sacred Mountain."
He diligently cultivated right awakening;
a strange stone came to be offered to him,
serving as a manifestation of his earnest sincerity.
Recorded as received.

On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, an imperial hand-written edict was bestowed. On the thirteenth day of the eighth month, one imperial hand-written edict was bestowed while [the Emperor] was at Mount Tai’s Jinguesi Temple. Imperial decree to Dharma Master Huixiao: [The text continues with the contents of the edict.]
The Emperor dispatched a central envoy to send Yang Shande there to oversee the meritorious works.
The Master devoted himself to meditation and recitation,
thereby benefiting his family and the state.
In the cool autumn, I hope you and your teachers are all well. This letter is brief; I have not much more to say. The 13th day.

A Memorial for Presenting the Merit of Performing Homa at Mount Wutai, together with a reply to the śramaṇa Huixiao. One memorial for presenting the merit of performing homa at Mount Wutai, along with the response to the śramaṇa Huixiao.
On the tenth day of the fourth month this year,
the imperial envoy Wei Mingxiu respectfully conveyed the Imperial Decree,

ordering the humble monk [name] to proceed to the Great Sage’s Golden Pavilion Baoying Zhenguo Temple on Mount Wutai to perform the merit of homa. The monk Huixiao, with sincere devotion and diligent application, fulfilled the Sacred Will.
Cultivating the aforementioned merits,
he invoked Mañjuśrī’s past vows and invoked the hidden power of his former masters.
There was a faint sense of reliance;
a resonance and image appeared in response.
Consequently, the fire attained a fresh and lustrous color without emitting smoke, differing from previous days and truly manifesting clear weather.
This is a sign of the peaceful tranquility of the realm and a verification that the dust of war has ceased.
All of this is due to Your Majesty’s subtle operation of the Ultimate Way and your virtue being in harmony with the High Heaven.
May the hundred spirits manifest their blessings,
may the myriad people rejoice in heart,
and may all demonic calamities be forever eliminated.
On this day of celebration and repose, I,
Huixiao, have the honor of being included among the ranks of the monastic community,
reverently receiving these enlightened instructions.
I am fearful of bringing disgrace upon Your Majesty’s decree.
May there be happiness and auspiciousness.
I am overcome with the utmost joy and celebration.
Respectfully submitted with this memorial by the imperial envoy Wei Mingxiu for the Emperor’s perusal.
Written with sincere joy and delight by the śramaṇa Huixiao.

Submitted on the eighteenth day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Dali by the śramaṇa Huixiao of Ximing Monastery to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, Martial and Civilly Wise. Imperial Rescript to the Great Sage Mañjuśrī:
To protect Mount Ling,
the Master’s heart of sincere devotion moved the divine spirits,
whose response was clearly manifest.
Sincerity must surely elicit a response;
this is deeply praiseworthy.
I am pleased to know of this.

Imperial Decree: To Fa-gao, the Metropolitan *Vaiyāvṛtyakara* of Daxingshan Monastery, regarding the decree that he shall continue to administer his duties as before. One decree, together with a formal notification, issued by imperial command to Li Yuancong: "Fa-gao, the Metropolitan *Vaiyāvṛtyakara* of Xingshan Monastery, shall be ordered to immediately continue to administer the affairs of the Metropolitan *Vaiyāvṛtyakara* as before."

On the seventeenth day of the fourth month in the tenth year of the Dali era, Li Xiancheng, a High Official (Gaopin), transmitted an imperial edict as the Commissioner for the Performance of Meritorious Deeds at the Various Temples and Observatories of the Capital. He issued a notification to Fa’gao, the Chief Steward (Du Weina) of Xingshan Monastery, stating: "I have received the notification that, in accordance with the aforementioned imperial edict, there has been no separate notification issued to the relevant authorities regarding its implementation. Therefore, I record this imperial edict and notify the monk Fa’gao. Thus was the notification issued on the seventeenth day of the fourth month in the tenth year of the Dali era. The Commissioner, Kai-fu Yitong Shisi, concurrently holding the office of Right Dragon Guard General, Li Cong, submitted a memorial of thanks for the imperial command to Master Youze to deliver a lecture at Xingshan Monastery. This consists of one memorial of thanks for the imperial command to Master Youze to deliver a lecture at Xingshan Monastery, along with a response from the śramaṇa Fa’gao and others.
I have reverently received the Imperial Edict of the fourth day of this month,
ordering the Dharma Master Youze of Zhangjing Monastery to lecture on the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* at that monastery.
The imperial favor descends like rain and dew upon my countenance, and the silken edicts overflow from [the Emperor’s] lips.
In the chronicle of the Buddha’s deeds,
the Dharma-sounds were formally proclaimed;
how could a mere speck of dust provide a ladder [to such heights]?
I am so cowed and anxious that I have no ground to stand upon.
I humbly submit that Your Majesty, the Emperor Baoying Yuansheng Wenwu,
governs the realm through benevolent transformation.
The esoteric practices and the upholding of the Dharma were transmitted eastward;
thus, [the Master] looked southward with concern. Furthermore, this monastery was established according to circumstances nearly two hundred years ago.
Although there have been no shortages of those who have held the office of *sōjūji* (abbot) throughout successive generations, such a proclamation of an imperial edict has never before been heard.
Now, the decree descends from heaven,
and the people emerge from the earth.
Although the sutras remain as they were of old,
the commentaries are truly new; thus,
the monks and nuns were commanded to hasten forth.
Men and women sought [the teaching] and flocked there like deer;
all this was due to the wondrous power of the Buddhas and the superior conditions provided by this sutra.
This fully expresses Your Majesty’s spirit of external protection and fulfills the monks’ rare fortune of encountering such patronage;
we earnestly hope it will further assist the imperial reign.
Strengthening the dignity of the state’s appearance,
may we bring the harvests of the years to a state of prosperity and peace,
and lead all living beings into the realm of longevity.
We are overcome with the utmost joy at this performance of dance.
We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude for your information.
The śramaṇas Fagong and others, filled with sincere joy and delight, respectfully state: [End of Text]

On the nineteenth day of the fourth month in the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the Śramaṇa Fagao, the Chief Steward (Upadhāyaka) of Daxingshan Monastery, submitted this memorial to the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, Martial and Civilly Virtuous. The Emperor’s decree was as follows: "The Master possesses exemplary conduct."
He cultivated sublime conduct with diligent effort,
opened the gates of expedient means,
and expounded the great principles of the Dharma.
He propagated the holy teachings to broaden the sublime causes,
fulfilling the loyal sincerity of his meritorious and worthy predecessors,
and elucidating the profound and subtle mysteries of the deep principles.
May all classes of sentient beings be equally bathed in auspicious blessings.
Your gratitude is acknowledged.

A Memorial of Thanks for the Imperial Decree Appointing the Śramaṇa Huilang as Abbot of Xingshan Temple; one memorial of thanks for the decree appointing the Śramaṇa Huilang as Abbot of Xingshan Temple, together with a response to the Śramaṇas Fagong and others.
I have reverently received the Imperial Edict of the fourteenth day of this month,
appointing the Venerable Huirang as the Senior Seat-Holder (Upādhyāya) of the Great Monastery.
It is illuminated by heavenly light.
Majesty and reverence are manifest upon his countenance;
this śramaṇa is a man of true character.
The era of the Semblance Dharma is about to endure long.
When the Dharma is heard by those of high standing,
it is what people desire;
Heaven will surely grant it.
The Way may perhaps still exist;
Your Majesty truly possesses the power [to restore it].
We humbly pray that Your Majesty, the Emperor, Treasure-Response, Primordial Sage, Martial and Civil, will take heed.
The Golden Wheel governs the course of fortune,
and the Jade Candle accords with the times;
thus, the Sage’s mind extends its external protection.
The compassionate grace of the Unconditioned descends;
those within the inner palace may keep it in mind and recite it without hindrance.
The temple is near the Celestial Street;
having secured its abbot without replacement,
I am overcome with the utmost joy and exultation.
I respectfully enclose this memorial, presented by Li Xiancheng, the Inner Official for Merit, to express our gratitude.
We, the śramaṇas Fagong and others, speak with sincere joy and delight.

On the fifteenth day of the fourth month in the thirteenth year of the Dali era, the śramaṇas Fagong and others, the General Steward (Du Weina) of Daxingshan Monastery, submit this memorial to His Majesty, the Emperor, the One of Precious Response, the Primordial Sage, the Martial and Civilly Wise. [The Emperor’s] Imperial Rescript: Your Eminences have purified the Garden of Brahmā with meticulous devotion.
Those who devote themselves to meditation and recitation and gather at the caityas must select and appoint those to oversee their discipline and administration.
Huìlǎng was reverent and diligent;
he truly lived up to the public selection and took charge of the temple affairs.
This is what is meant by "attaining a person. I humbly submit this for your perusal.

The Stele for the Tripiṭaka Master and Upādhyāya Bukong (Amoghavajra), Posthumously Honored as Grand Minister of Works (Sikong), Great Distinguished Debater (Dàbiànzhèng), and of Vast Wisdom (Guǎngzhì). One Stele for the Tripiṭaka Upādhyāya at his own Monastery. The Stele Inscription for the National Teacher, the Tripiṭaka Master of Great Xingshan Temple, the Great Distinguished Debater of Vast Wisdom. Title: *Stele Inscription with Preface for the Late Virtuous One, the Tripiṭaka Upādhyāya of Great Xingshan Temple, the Great Distinguished Debater of Vast Wisdom*. Composed by Yan Ying, Silver Light Merit and Honor (Yīnguāng Lùdàfū), Censor-in-Chief (Yǔshì Dàfū), Upper Pillar State (Shàngzhùguó), and Marquis of Kāiyí County. Calligraphed by Xu Huo, Silver Light Merit and Honor, Court Gentleman for the Prince of Penglai (Péngwáng Zhàn), Upper Pillar State, and Marquis of Kuàijī Commandery. The Upādhyāya’s name was Bukong.
He was a man from the Western Regions.
As his clan name was not known in the Middle Kingdom, it is not recorded here.
The Xuanzong Emperor, who possessed the insight to perceive the Ultimate Way, held him in exceptional esteem and veneration.
He served as State Preceptor for the Consecration Rite (*abhiṣeka*) during the three reigns of Emperors Suzong and Daizong.
By means of his profound words and virtuous auspiciousness, he provided protection and guidance to the Supreme Sovereign.
At the beginning of Daizong’s reign...
He was honored with the title of Tèjìn (Special Advance) and Dàhónglú (Grand Minister of State Ceremonial), as recorded in the official tablets.
When he manifested illness and ceased to rise from his bed,
